# S169 — Per-vendor slot cap and vendor-out memory (one Codex slot, Claude stand-in)

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-10-29** — Owner decisions 2026-10-29 (interactive): a vendor marked out after a rate-limit or out-of-credits exit stays out for 60 minutes (fixed expiry) or until `ork vendor back`, and a daemon restart clears it (supersedes the spec's until-back default); a run waiting for a full vendor slot keeps its global-cap slot; with the vendor out and no other-vendor row the round tries the row anyway; built-in cap codex 1, claude unlimited, no registry field.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**2026-10-30** — Review FAIL (review round 1, 2026-10-29): a round waiting for the codex slot still runs its codex row after the slot holder went out, because the holder releases the slot before it marks the vendor out (round.go release before MarkOut) and the waiter picked its row before the wait. Fix round 1 moves the mark before the release and re-picks the row after a waited acquire.

## Why

Owner policy: one Codex slot at a time, and a Claude sonnet-high stand-in when Codex is out of credits. ork cannot apply either today, so the owner applies both by hand.

What ork does now:
- Fallback is per round. An exit classified `rate_limited` or `error` moves the role to the next row of its chain (`internal/engine/round.go:329-355`, adj 156 vendor.fallback-trigger-v2); the role stays on that row for the run (adj 115 vendor.fallback-sticky, `internal/engine/engine.go:171-203`). The Codex classifier reads "You've hit your usage limit", "out of credits" and HTTP 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` as rate limited (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go:194`).
- The caps count runs, not vendors: the global cap and the project cap count busy runs (`internal/daemon/runs.go:722-746`, adj 20 wave.limits, adj 122 wave.slots). Two parallel runs can both be on Codex.
- Nothing remembers that a vendor is out. Each new run, and each new run's later rounds, tries Codex first and falls back again, spending a failed round each time.
- Claude has no measured rate-limit class (`internal/agent/claude/types.go:24-28`, `vendor.unsampled-classes`); a Claude limit shows as `error`, which still falls back. This slice does not change that: no sample exists to classify.

Parity row: 2.4 and gap 4 of the prioritized list in `docs/orchestrator-parity.md` (from S165).

Owner decisions that apply: fallback is automatic (adj 22); the role matrix and its row order are slicer's and ork never edits them (`docs/boundaries.md`); slicer s405 gives the orchestrator-side rule for the same event (on out of credits skip later rows on the same vendor, on a rate limit take the next matching row), which ork's engine mirrors here for its own roles. ork adds no dependency.

Slicer check (`slicer find "vendor cap" --root ../slicer`, `"slot"`, `"out of credits"`): slicer has s405 (done, the fallback rule in the relay contract) and s215 (caps new implementation pickups for slicer's own queue). Neither limits a vendor's concurrent roles nor remembers a vendor as out, and neither runs ork's roles. This slice is ork's own engine and daemon.

Design (*proposed*):
- A shared in-memory `Vendors` value in `engine.Deps` (like `Landings`, `internal/engine/landlock.go`). Nil means no cap and no memory, so existing tests do not change.
- Slot cap per vendor, enforced per role round: a round that would start a vendor process first acquires that vendor's slot and releases it when the process ends. Built-in default: codex 1, claude unlimited. Rounds on a full vendor wait, oldest first. The wait is before the ledger step and the role record, so it does not count against the run's time budget.
- Vendor-out memory: a round that exits `rate_limited` marks its vendor out, with the time and the exit text. An `error` exit does not. While a vendor is out, a round that starts on one of its rows takes the next row of the chain on another vendor, if there is one; if there is none it tries the row anyway (as today). The memory is in the daemon only and lasts until the owner clears it or the daemon restarts (see Open). The owner can also mark a vendor out before a round fails.
- The plan notes a vendor that is out. `ork status` and the TUI status line show it. `ork vendor [list]`, `ork vendor out NAME`, `ork vendor back NAME` set and clear it. A run that waits for a slot says so on its Running row.

Not in this slice: a registry field for caps (file-format change, with gap 7.2), classifying Claude limits, a time-based expiry (Open), freeing the run's global slot while it waits (Open), spec-check rounds (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:193-231` keeps its own chain), the hung-role watchdog (S182).

## Failing tests

- `TestVendorSlotsLimitHoldersPerVendorAndLeaveOthersAlone` (`internal/engine/vendors_test.go`): with codex 1, a second `Acquire("codex")` blocks until the first releases; `claude` is unlimited; a nil `Vendors` never blocks.
- `TestVendorSlotWaitersGoInArrivalOrderAndStopOnCancel`: three waiters are served oldest first; a cancelled wait returns `ctx.Err()` and frees its place.
- `TestRoundWaitsForTheVendorSlotWithoutSpendingBudget` (`internal/engine/fallback_test.go`): a second run's codex round waits while the first holds the slot, the run reports the wait, and the waited minutes are not in `overBudget`.
- `TestStopWhileWaitingForAVendorSlotStopsTheRun`: `Stop` during the wait ends the run with no role record and no ledger step.
- `TestRateLimitedExitMarksTheVendorOutAndErrorDoesNot`: a `rate_limited` codex exit marks codex out; an `error` exit falls back but marks nothing.
- `TestNewRoundSkipsRowsOfAVendorThatIsOut`: with codex out, a new run's implementer starts on the first claude row; `currentEntry` agrees on later rounds and after a reopen (the later row's record matches forward).
- `TestOutVendorWithNoOtherVendorRowStillRunsTheRow`: a chain of codex rows only still runs the first row.
- `TestPlanNotesAVendorThatIsOut` (`internal/daemon/vendors_test.go`): `run.plan` carries a `note` naming the vendor, its time and `ork vendor back NAME`; `run.start` with the earlier `Expected` is refused as changed.
- `TestVendorsListSetAndBackOverTheWire`: `vendors.set` marks and clears; `vendors.list`, `status` and `snapshot` carry the out vendors; a vendor other than `claude` or `codex` is `bad_params`.
- `TestDaemonSharesOneVendorsValueAndDefaultsCodexToOne`: two runs of one daemon share the cap; the default is codex 1.
- `TestVendorCommandListsMarksAndClears` (`internal/cli/vendor_test.go`): `ork vendor`, `ork vendor out codex`, `ork vendor back codex`, usage errors exit 2, `--json` prints one value.
- `TestStatusLineAndRunningRowShowVendorState` (`internal/tui/vendors_test.go`): the status line shows `codex out since HH:MM` in the warning colour; a waiting run's Running row line 2 says `waits for the codex slot`; goldens at 100x30 (`vendor-out-100x30-mono.txt`, `-color.txt`).

## Implement

UI slice: UI pass (r14). Test-first: write the tests above, see them fail, then:
1. `internal/engine/vendors.go` (new): `type Vendors` with `NewVendors(caps map[string]int)`, `Acquire(ctx, vendor) (release func(), waited bool, err error)` (arrival-ordered waiters, cap 0 or missing means unlimited; pattern of `Landings.Acquire`, `internal/engine/landlock.go:32`), `MarkOut(vendor, reason string, at time.Time)`, `Back(vendor)`, `IsOut(vendor) bool`, `Out() []VendorOut{Vendor, Reason, Since}` sorted by vendor. Nil-safe methods. `Deps.Vendors *Vendors` at `internal/engine/engine.go:45-60`.
2. `internal/engine/round.go:179-187`: after `entryIndex := currentEntry(rec, r.role)`, advance past rows whose vendor is out to the first later row of a vendor that is not out; if none, keep the index. `currentEntry` (`engine.go:171`) needs no change: it scans forward, so the later row's record matches (a test pins this).
3. `internal/engine/round.go:262-269`: before `stepStart`, `release, waited, err := e.d.Vendors.Acquire(ctx, entry.Vendor)`; while waiting, set the engine's wait marker (`Engine.VendorWait() string`, memory only, like `Live()`); on a cancelled ctx return as the other cancelled paths do (`:293-306`). `defer release()` ends after `endActivity()` (`:292`). The wait is before the role record (`:273`), so `overBudget` (`:145`) never sees it. The sibling reviewer and UI rounds of one state may both need a slot; each holds one vendor slot only, so there is no cycle.
4. `internal/engine/round.go:329-355`: when `class == ExitRateLimited`, call `e.d.Vendors.MarkOut(entry.Vendor, reason, e.d.now())` with the round's exit text; not for `ExitError`.
5. `internal/daemon/runs.go:149-158`: `initRunManager` creates one `engine.Vendors` with `defaultVendorCaps = {"codex": 1}` (*proposed*) when `deps.Vendors` is nil, so every run of the daemon shares it. `runs.go:333-483` (`planRun`): append to `plan.Note` when a vendor in any chain is out. `runs.go:1236-1262`: fill `EngineRun.VendorWait` from the engine.

Order: independent of S166, S167, S168. S182 edits the same `runRound` (`round.go:285-306`) around the runner call: land either first and rebase; they touch different lines.
Not verified: whether `Engine.Stop` can take the engine lock while a round waits (the wait runs inside `Run`, which holds `Engine.mu` while the runner streams, per `internal/engine/activity.go:14`); `TestStopWhileWaitingForAVendorSlotStopsTheRun` decides it and may need the wait to sit outside the lock.
Open: (a) How long is a vendor out? Recommended: until the owner runs `ork vendor back` or the daemon restarts, because the classifier cannot tell a 429, a usage window and out of credits apart (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go:194`; adj 51 records that the usage-limit text can appear with quota left). Options: a fixed expiry such as 60 minutes plus `back`; or a single probe after N minutes. (b) A run waiting for a full slot keeps its global-cap slot (recommended: simplest, and the wait is bounded by one role round). The option is to hand the global slot back while it waits, which changes adj 122. The other option is to use the next chain row instead of waiting, which is not the owner's policy. (c) With the vendor out and no other-vendor row in the chain: try the row anyway (recommended, as today), or pause the run for the owner. (d) Caps: built-in codex 1 (recommended, no file-format change); or an optional registry `vendor_caps` field, which the strict-key registry rules (`internal/registry/registry.go:134-148`) turn into a version bump, best done with gap 7.2.

Owner decisions 2026-10-29 (interactive, review round 1): an owner mark (ork vendor out) has no expiry and holds until ork vendor back or a daemon restart; only exit marks expire after 60 minutes. The Running row wait text is waits for codex. While vendor_wait is set the heard cell is dim with no ! or !! cue (a ledger heartbeat during the wait is a later slice). Wording leads with the end: status line codex out until 17:02 (an owner mark reads codex out until back); ork status, ork vendor and the plan note read codex is out until HH:MM (since HH:MM; reason).
